Wraps & materials · 6 minute read

How to look after a vehicle wrap.

How to wash a wrapped van, which products to use and avoid, how to deal with fuel, tar and bird droppings, and what to do if an edge lifts.

Get a free quote ↗Try the Van Designer ↗

At a glance

1week before the first wash
2buckets for hand washing
0pressure washer on the edges

In this guide

  1. The first week after fitting
  2. Washing a wrapped van
  3. Stains, damage and quick repairs
Get a free quote ↗

Quick answer

Leave the wrap to settle before the first wash, hand wash with a mild shampoo, keep pressure washers well back and away from edges, and avoid polishes or waxes not made for vinyl.

01

The first week after fitting

The adhesive on a new wrap keeps bonding to the paint for a few days after fitting. Give it time to settle before washing, and avoid parking against hedges or walls that could catch the edges.

Tip

We will give you the exact aftercare advice for your film when you collect your van.

02

Washing a wrapped van

1

Hand wash

Use a soft mitt, two buckets and a pH-neutral vehicle shampoo.

2

Pressure wash with care

Keep the lance well back, at a low angle, and never aim at edges or seams.

3

Dry gently

Use a soft microfibre towel or let it air dry out of direct sun.

Use

  • pH-neutral shampoo
  • Soft wash mitts and microfibre
  • Products labelled vinyl or wrap safe
  • Cold or lukewarm water

Avoid

  • Brush car washes
  • Solvents, polishes and cutting compounds
  • Wax on matte or satin films
  • Scrapers or stiff brushes
03

Stains, damage and quick repairs

Fuel, tar, tree sap and bird droppings can mark film if they are left to bake in the sun. Clean them off as soon as you can with water and a mild cleaner made for vinyl.

Leaving bird droppings

They can etch the film in hot weather.

Fix: Soak and wipe them off quickly.

Picking at a lifted edge

Pulling makes it worse and lets dirt in.

Fix: Call us and we will reseal or replace it.

Polishing matte film

Polish leaves shiny patches.

Fix: Use matte-safe products only.

What to have ready for your quote

  • Date the wrap was fitted
  • Film type and finish
  • Wash method you use
  • Where the van is parked
  • Any lifting edges
  • Photos of any damage
  • Fuel or chemical spills
  • Your contact details

Before you book

Vehicle wrap aftercare: your questions.

When can I wash my van after fitting?

Give the wrap about a week to settle before the first wash, then hand wash it gently. We confirm the exact time for your film when you collect.

Can I use a brush car wash?

It is best avoided. Brushes can scratch the film and catch edges. Hand washing or a touchless wash used carefully is safer.

What do I do if an edge lifts?

Do not pull it. Keep it clean and give us a call: we can usually reseal or replace the panel quickly.
